title: Add invocation cohort tiling and sampled log quantizer
author: Ayesha Gupta
description:
Motivation: Long-tail invocation noise and high-cardinality log payloads make it expensive to retain full context for every request. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) 'Invocation cohort tiling' — a light-weight bucketing strategy that groups similar invocations into stable cohorts for aggregation, and 2) 'Sampled log quantizer' — a tunable quantization layer that reduces log cardinality before storage while preserving representative examples for debugging. The two systems together aim to reduce telemetry storage and query cost by ~30% on average for chat-heavy workloads while keeping actionable debugging context for incidents.

What changed (high-level): Added a cohort tiler that computes a small deterministic cohort key from invocation fingerprint features (route, model-family, prompt-shape-hash, tenant-tier). Cohort keys are exposed as invocation.metadata.cohort_tier and emitted as metrics labels where low-cardinality is required. Implemented a sampled_log_quantizer that applies configurable quantization buckets and string interning to logs marked as sampleable. Introduced new rollout gates and feature flags so we can toggle quantization per-tenant and per-route.

Description of key behaviors: The cohort tiler produces 1 of ~256 tiles by default; tiles are stable across restarts and are computed via a two-stage hash with salt derived from deployment id. The sampled_log_quantizer supports three modes: pass-through, coarse-quantize (trim rare tokens and collapse numeric ranges), and representative-sample (keep top-k unique samples and replace others with a sample-id). Both components include annotation hooks so traces retain pointers to exact log objects when requested.

Files of interest and config knobs: config/obs/cohort_tiler.yaml (default 256 tiles, allowlist routes), config/obs/log_quantizer.yaml (mode, per-tenant overrides, top_k_sample_size), server/telemetry/cohort_tiler.go, server/telemetry/quantizer.go, telemetry/docs/observability-tiling.md.

Testing and validation: Unit tests covering deterministic tiling and quantizer transforms; synthetic replay bench that verifies latency overhead < 1ms p95 at 64 concurrency; integration test that verifies metric rollups produced by cohort tags and end-to-end retention reduction on staging. We ran a 2-week canary on preview tenants (10 tenants) that showed median storage reduction 28% and no increase in incident MTTR during post-canary drills.

Rollout plan: Start with feature off for all tenants. Enable use_flag 'obs.cohort_tiling' for internal-preview tenants + opt-in customers. After 7 days and no regressions, enable sampled_log_quantizer in coarse mode for non-enterprise tenants. Provide per-tenant overrides in the console. Documented rollback steps in telemetry/docs/rollback-tiler.md.

Impact and migration notes: Metrics that include invocation.metadata.cohort_tier are low-cardinality by construction; dashboards that want cohort-level breakdowns should include the cohort_tier label. Existing dashboards that do not expect the label will be unaffected. The sampled log quantizer is opt-in by config and does not change original log storage unless explicitly enabled for a tenant.

Risks and mitigations: There is a risk of over-aggregation hiding root-cause signals for very narrow-but-critical tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant allowlist and ability to mark routes as 'do-not-quantize'. We also emit an index mapping from cohort tile -> representative fingerprints for 14 days to aid forensic queries.

Notes for reviewers: look at deterministic hashing, salting, and the tests for collision distribution. Also verify the production readiness of the feature flags and console toggles. Related: ENG-2483 (observability cost containment), ENG-2490 (long-tail log reduction).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice approach to keep cohort cardinality bounded. Question: how was 256 chosen as default? Can we make it dynamic based on tenant size?

Ayesha Gupta: 256 was chosen from distro tests (see cohort_tiler_test) as a good default for our mixing; we added a tenant-level override so large tenants can increase to 1024 in the config. Will add note in docs.
Evelyn Chen: Please add a short comment in quantizer.go explaining the safety properties for numeric bucketing (so future devs don't accidentally change range semantics).
Ayesha Gupta: Added comments and an extra unit test covering numeric edge cases.
Ravi Patel: CI flaked once on bench due to build environment; re-ran and it's green. Approving after small nits addressed.
Diego Morales: Approving — verified no metric label explosion in staging and storage delta matches bench numbers.
release_notes:
- Introduce invocation cohort tiling (stable, low-cardinality cohort_id) for aggregated telemetry; default 256 tiles, per-tenant override.
- Add sampled log quantizer with 3 modes (pass-through, coarse-quantize, representative-sample) to reduce log cardinality and storage.
- Add console toggles and per-route allowlist for telemetry quantization.
Notes: Opt-in for tenants; monitor storage and MTTR when enabling.
notes_for_ops: Rollout steps: enable obs.cohort_tiling for preview tenants via console flag, monitor telemetry.storage.delta and invocation.slo.slack for 72h, then enable quantizer coarse mode for remaining non-SLA tenants. Rollback: flip flags off; run rehydration script to re-index any required representative samples (see telemetry/docs/rollback-tiler.md).
